edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Seller’s proposed purchase price for the Shares is USD 45,000,000, subject to agreement on valuation assumptions and customary adjustments for cash, debt, working capital against an agreed normalized target, and unpaid transaction expenses, without double counting. The parties shall agree applicable definitions, accounting principles, an illustrative calculation, completion-account procedures and an independent-accountant dispute mechanism. The Buyer’s USD 35,000,000 proposal remains under discussion and is not accepted by this draft. No price or transaction commitment shall arise unless definitive agreements are executed following the parties’ respective approvals.

2. Closing; Interim Covenants; Termination. The parties shall target Closing within 30 days after signing, subject to completion of satisfactory diligence before execution of definitive agreements, necessary corporate and regulatory approvals and third-party consents, and satisfaction or permitted waiver of agreed closing conditions. Any diligence condition continuing after signing must be expressly agreed, with defined scope and timing. Closing conditions shall include the accuracy of representations, subject to agreed materiality standards, and material performance of pre-closing covenants. Before Closing, the Seller shall procure operation of the business in the ordinary course, preservation of material business relationships, reasonable diligence access subject to confidentiality, privilege and applicable law, and restrictions on material extraordinary transactions, distributions, indebtedness and disposals, with agreed exceptions and Buyer consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. The parties shall cooperate in obtaining approvals and consents. Definitive agreements shall provide termination rights for mutual consent, failure to close by an agreed outside date, a final legal prohibition, and an uncured material breach preventing satisfaction of a closing condition, subject to appropriate notice and cure periods. A party may not rely on a failure it caused through its own material breach. Termination shall preserve agreed surviving provisions and liability for prior actionable breaches.

3. Representations; Indemnification. Definitive agreements shall contain customary Seller representations concerning title to the Shares, authority and enforceability, capitalization, financial statements, undisclosed liabilities, tax, material contracts, litigation, compliance with law, and other matters reasonably identified through diligence, with appropriate scope, materiality and knowledge qualifications and disclosure-schedule exceptions. Subject to applicable accounting standards and agreed qualifications, the financial statements shall fairly present the financial position and results of the business. The Seller shall provide indemnification for breaches of its representations and covenants and agreed pre-Closing tax liabilities, subject to negotiated survival periods, thresholds, deductibles, caps, claims procedures, mitigation and no-double-recovery provisions. Meaningful recourse shall be provided through an agreed escrow or holdback, with its amount, duration and release mechanics to be negotiated. Fundamental representations, tax claims and fraud shall receive separately agreed treatment, subject to applicable law. No unlimited indemnity or specific escrow amount is agreed by this draft.

4. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep confidential the negotiations, this Agreement and non-public information received concerning the other party or the business, and shall use such information solely to evaluate, finance or implement the proposed transaction. Disclosure is permitted to representatives, professional advisers and bona fide financing sources with a need to know who are subject to appropriate confidentiality duties, and as required by law, regulation, court order or applicable stock-exchange rules. For required disclosures, the disclosing party shall, to the extent legally permitted and reasonably practicable, give advance notice, cooperate in seeking protective treatment and disclose only what is required. Customary exclusions shall apply to information that is public other than through breach, lawfully obtained without restriction, previously lawfully known, or independently developed. Existing confidentiality agreements remain effective, with any conflicts to be expressly resolved in definitive documentation.

receiver.message_back:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for the revised draft. The expanded transaction protections provide a useful basis for further drafting. They do not, however, establish support for the Seller's USD 45,000,000 valuation. The Buyer maintains its USD 35,000,000 proposal, subject to satisfactory diligence, definitive documentation and required approvals. We acknowledge that the Seller has not accepted it; neither price should be presented as agreed.

Our principal valuation assumptions are sustainable, supportable earnings and cash generation; a normalized level of working capital; and appropriate adjustments for cash, debt, debt-like liabilities and unpaid transaction expenses, without double counting. Please confirm whether the Seller's asking price is an enterprise-value or equity-value figure and provide its valuation methodology and supporting bridge. Our proposal should not be understood as accepting any presently unspecified adjustment methodology or valuation multiple.

Our initial diligence priorities are:
• Three years of financial statements, current management accounts, budgets and forecasts, with reconciliations and support for earnings adjustments.
• Monthly working-capital information, receivables aging, inventory quality, cash, borrowings, debt-like obligations and transaction expenses.
• Revenue quality, customer concentration, material contracts, change-of-control provisions and required consents.
• Tax exposures, litigation, regulatory compliance, capitalization, share title and material contingent liabilities.

Please open the confidential data room and provide an index and proposed diligence timetable. Privileged material need not be disclosed; where restrictions apply, please identify the affected categories and propose lawful alternatives, including redactions or non-privileged summaries.

For the next draft, please develop the completion-account definitions and dispute process, closing conditions and outside date, detailed representations and disclosure schedules, and meaningful indemnity recourse supported by an escrow or holdback. The scope and economics of those protections remain open pending diligence. The 30-day closing target should depend on the necessary approvals and consents, rather than operate as an unconditional deadline.

The Buyer is prepared to progress diligence promptly. All discussions remain subject to contract and approvals, with existing confidentiality obligations preserved.

Kind regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP
